title: PolicyReports are now one per resource, named by UID, instead of one per policy
quote: Policy Reports are now created on a _per-resource_ basis and using a UID as the name rather than the previous behavior of _per-policy_.
remediation: Update dashboards, alerts and scripts that read PolicyReports by name or expect one report per policy (Policy Reporter, custom exporters). Reports are now named by the resource UID and removed with the resource.
verifyCommand: kubectl get policyreports.wgpolicyk8s.io -A --no-headers 2>/dev/null | head -5  # rows are current reports; after 1.11 their names are resource UIDs
coversNotes: Blog: Policy Report Enhancements (With the introduction of Kyverno 1.11)

title: Cosign 2.0: image verification needs an explicit Rekor URL (or ignoreTlogs / ignoreSCT)

detection.reason: verifyImages attestor settings are not collected

quote: In accordance with Cosign 2.0 updates, the Rekor URL is now required in a policy.
remediation: Keyed cosign signatures without a transparency-log entry now fail verification (a missing `rekor` block means the public Rekor). For images signed without Rekor set `rekor.ignoreTlog: true` and `ctlog.ignoreSCT: true` on the attestor (the field is `ignoreTlog` — a misspelt field is pruned silently by the API server); otherwise the Pods are blocked.
verifyCommand: kubectl get clusterpolicies.kyverno.io,policies.kyverno.io -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | select(any(.spec.rules[]?.verifyImages[]?.attestors[]?.entries[]?; has("keys") and (.keys.rekor == null))) | "\(.kind) \(.metadata.namespace // "-")/\(.metadata.name)"'  # each row has a cosign key attestor without a rekor block

title: PolicyExceptions are enabled by default — existing exceptions start exempting resources

detection.reason: read from the kyverno.io PolicyExceptions in the cluster

quote: Changed the default value of `--enablePolicyException` from `false` to `true`.
remediation: Review the PolicyExceptions named: from 1.11 they take effect unless the admission controller runs with `--enablePolicyException=false`. Restrict who can create PolicyExceptions (RBAC) and, from 1.13, the namespace they may live in.
verifyCommand: kubectl get policyexceptions.kyverno.io -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | "\(.kind) \(.metadata.namespace // "-")/\(.metadata.name)"'  # each row is an exception that becomes active
coversNotes: v1.11.0 Changed: Policy Exceptions are now enabled by default (#8545)

title: The JSON patch implementation was replaced — some mutations behave slightly differently

detection.reason: mutate rule patches are not collected

quote: Replaced the internal package used to apply JSON patches. This resulted in some fixes and slight behavioral changes (#7401, #7452)
remediation: Re-test mutate rules that use `patchesJson6902` (especially array index and `remove` operations) in a staging cluster before upgrading.
verifyCommand: kubectl get clusterpolicies.kyverno.io,policies.kyverno.io -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | select(any(.spec.rules[]?.mutate?; .patchesJson6902 != null)) | "\(.kind) \(.metadata.namespace // "-")/\(.metadata.name)"'  # each row uses JSON 6902 patches

title: Kyverno no longer writes the `policies.kyverno.io/last-applied-patches` annotation

detection.reason: tooling that reads the annotation lives outside the cluster

quote: The `policies.kyverno.io/last-applied-patches` annotation upon successful mutation has been removed (#7438)
remediation: Stop relying on the annotation in scripts or audits; use PolicyReports or Kyverno events to see which mutations applied.
coversNotes: v1.11.0 Helm: #7438 chore: remove last-applied-patches annotation

title: Enforce no longer blocks an UPDATE of a resource that already violated the rule the same way (1.11.2, 1.12.0)

detection.reason: whether a resource violated a rule before the upgrade is not collected

quote: Fixed an issue allowing changes to pre-existing resources in violation of a Validation policy in Enforce mode (#9027)
remediation: Expect pre-existing violators to stay editable: an UPDATE whose validation result is the same as the old object's is now skipped instead of denied (d3d0eb354, `IsSameRuleResponse` → skip). Policies that relied on blocking every change to a non-compliant resource — e.g. the `restrict-scale` sample on `Deployment/scale` — stop doing so; read PolicyReports to find the existing violators and fix them directly.
verifyCommand: kubectl get clusterpolicies.kyverno.io,policies.kyverno.io -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | select((.spec.validationFailureAction // "" | test("(?i)enforce")) or any(.spec.rules[]?.validate?; (.failureAction // "") | test("(?i)enforce"))) | "\(.kind) \(.metadata.namespace // "-")/\(.metadata.name)"'  # each row is a policy that enforces

title: Policies on `Deployment/scale` (restrict-scale sample) must use a condition anchor (from 1.11.2)

detection.reason: read from the kinds named in each policy's match blocks

quote: The policy that applies to `Deployment/scale` subresource has been changed to use condition anchor for the condition check.
remediation: Update policies copied from `restrict-scale` to the current library version (condition anchor) or they stop blocking scale actions.
